name: Growth and market-entry strategy
summary: Where to compete, how to win, and in what order: a growth plan your board can commit capital to.
overview: Growth decisions are rarely short of ideas. They are short of evidence, sequence and the discipline to say no. We help leadership teams choose where to play, test whether the opportunity is as large and as reachable as it looks, and turn the choice into a plan with owners, milestones and capital attached.

Because our strategy work sits beside our risk, regulatory and transactions practices, each option is judged on what it could earn and on what it could cost if it goes wrong, in one conversation rather than three.
when: You are deciding whether to enter a new state, segment, channel or country
Growth has stalled and the board wants an independent view of why
Several expansion options compete for the same capital
An investor or lender wants a defensible business plan

Customer, channel and competitor research, including expert interviews
Option appraisal: economics, capabilities, regulatory hurdles and risks
Build, partner or buy analysis for each route to market

approach: Clarify the ambition, constraints and the decision the board must take.
Gather evidence on markets, customers and competitors; size each option honestly.

Translate the choice into a plan your team owns, and help launch it.

Market model and option appraisal you can update

outcomes: A growth choice the board can defend

name: M&A advisory, buy side and sell side
summary: Senior support from first approach to closing, so the deal you sign is the deal you intended.
overview: A transaction compresses years of strategy into weeks of negotiation. We act for buyers and sellers to frame the rationale, identify and approach counterparties, shape the structure and keep the process moving, with the same senior people at the table throughout.
Our advice is independent of who finances or completes the deal. We are as willing to tell you to walk away as to sign.

A counterparty has approached you and you need to respond well
A promoter is planning succession or a partial exit
A process has stalled and needs a fresh, senior hand

name: Commercial, financial and integrity due diligence
summary: What the numbers, the market and the people behind a deal are really telling you, before you commit.
overview: Due diligence is no longer a box to tick before signing; increasingly it is the decision itself. We examine the business you are buying or backing from three angles at once: whether its market and customers support the plan, whether its earnings and cash are what they appear to be, and whether its promoters, partners and practices can be trusted.
Findings are sourced, graded for reliability and written for decision-makers, with the price, structure and protection implications spelt out.
when: You are about to invest in, lend to or acquire a business
A seller's numbers or growth story feel too good
A target has related parties, complex ownership or a history you cannot see
Your board or investment committee needs an independent view quickly

Financial diligence: quality of earnings, net debt, working capital and cash conversion
Integrity diligence: promoters, ownership, related parties, litigation and reputation
Red-flag reviews on short timelines
Price, structure and warranty implications for each finding
approach: Agree the questions that would change your decision, and focus there.
Data room, management sessions, public records, interviews and site visits.
Challenge every claim against independent evidence.
Clear findings, how sure we are, and what to do about each.

name: International due diligence and background checks
summary: Knowing who you are dealing with, wherever in the world they are.
overview: Partners, targets and executives abroad can be hard to assess from India. We carry out international due diligence and background checks using public records, corporate registries, litigation and regulatory sources, media and lawful enquiries, through our network across jurisdictions.
Findings are sourced, graded for reliability and written so decision-makers can act.
when: You are entering a partnership or deal with a foreign party
You are appointing a senior executive with an international history
A counterparty's ownership or reputation is unclear
Sanctions or anti-bribery rules require checks
what: Corporate and beneficial ownership research
Litigation, regulatory and sanctions checks
Adverse media and reputation reviews
Executive and promoter background checks
Discreet lawful enquiries where permitted
approach: The questions that matter for your decision.
Records, registries and sources across jurisdictions.
